question: Can a reasoning language model learn which of its own KV-cache blocks to evict, jointly with token generation and from the same outcome reward, while maintaining accuracy under a fixed periodic memory budget?

key_findings.claim: NGC turns per-layer KV-cache retention into a stochastic policy action parameterized by the model's existing attention scores.
key_findings.evidence: At a fixed cadence, the last five queries score prefix keys, scores are averaged across heads/queries and pooled into contiguous 32-token blocks, and Gumbel top-k samples a fixed-size retained subset independently in every transformer layer. No new policy parameters are introduced.

key_findings.claim: Token and eviction actions receive the same group-relative binary task advantage, but the amount and timing of memory reduction are manually fixed rather than learned.
key_findings.evidence: The objective sums token and eviction policy-gradient terms with a shared Dr. GRPO advantage. Yet cadence, per-round eviction fraction, block size, and curriculum are external hyperparameters; the resource constraint enters by construction, not through a learned cost tradeoff.

anchors.section: Eviction policy gradient and total objective

key_findings.claim: The described replay construction reproduces the state-shifted context seen during rollout and keeps eviction decisions on the autograd graph.
key_findings.evidence: Because evicted tokens were unavailable to later queries, ordinary causal-mask rescoring would be off-policy. The construction uses per-layer, query-dependent visibility masks and recomputes the relevant Q/K features in the replay forward pass, so the derivation permits gradients from eviction log-probabilities to reach all model parameters. The paper does not release a numerical replay-equivalence test, so this verifies the stated construction rather than an external implementation.

key_findings.claim: The claim that replay masks add negligible overhead is not established by a measured systems comparison.
key_findings.evidence: The implementation constructs dense Boolean B-by-T-by-T masks separately for every layer because visibility is query-dependent. The paper reports no training wall-clock, peak total GPU memory, attention-kernel efficiency, or comparison against standard Dr. GRPO, so 'no additional overhead' is an algorithmic assertion rather than a systems result.

key_findings.claim: On Countdown at 2.4x reported peak-cache reduction, NGC substantially beats the four inference-only heuristics.
key_findings.evidence: Pass@1 is 49.6% for NGC versus 21.2% KeyDiff, 7.8% SnapKV, 0.2% StreamingLLM, and 0.1% KNorm, while the full-cache ceiling is roughly 64%. Error bars are one standard error, but independent training seeds are not reported.

key_findings.claim: Countdown ablations show that correct state replay and an explicit eviction policy gradient both matter in this implementation.
key_findings.evidence: Targeted KV Dropout, which trains with eviction but naively rescored causal context, reaches 2.5% and collapses near step 100; replay masks with token log-probabilities but no eviction loss reach 35.7%; full NGC reaches 49.6%. This isolates two components but not the comparison to prior learned compression training.

key_findings.claim: Budget-aware interoception improves accuracy at aggressive caches, but it assumes the deployment budget is known and encoded in the prompt.
key_findings.evidence: Adding an eviction-rate tag during training and testing produces an 8-13 point gain at strict budgets and extrapolates below the minimum training cache. This is useful conditional control, not autonomous budget discovery or adaptation to unknown resource pressure.

key_findings.claim: On held-out math competitions, NGC's pass@32 curves dominate the four heuristic baselines at the tested aggressive settings, but the evidence has no uncertainty and only one 1.5B model.
key_findings.evidence: At 50% eviction per round, approximate Figure 7 values are 70% on AMC23, 61% on AMC25, and 21.5% on AIME25 for NGC, with every heuristic lower. Figure 8 shows a favorable 2-3x tradeoff and nonmonotonic AIME behavior at more aggressive ratios. No seed bars or significance tests accompany these small-benchmark pass@32 estimates.

key_findings.claim: The reported average peak-cache-reduction ratio is confounded by method-dependent completion length.
key_findings.evidence: Its numerator uses prompt plus the no-eviction baseline's completion length, whereas its denominator uses the evaluated method's own completion length. A method that generates shorter or longer reasoning receives a different ratio even under the same cache rule, so models are not matched on generated-token budget.

key_findings.claim: The baseline comparison mixes training regimes and omits the closest learned and RL-guided predecessors.
key_findings.evidence: NGC is trained with cache deletion, whereas the four reported heuristics are applied only at inference to a full-cache-trained model. This does not isolate the proposed discrete policy action from generic compression-aware exposure or additional training compute. DMS, Breadcrumbs, DMC, MEMENTO, and especially RLKV are absent: RLKV v1 predates NGC by more than six months and already uses GRPO outcome rewards from generated reasoning to optimize per-head full-versus-local-cache gates, although it freezes the LM, adds an L1 sparsity penalty, and performs offline head selection rather than native per-round token eviction.

key_findings.claim: NGC evaluates a KV-memory proxy but not practical inference efficiency.
key_findings.evidence: There are no tokens/s, time-to-first-token, latency, batch-throughput, total GPU-memory, wall-clock, energy, or FLOP measurements. Blockwise selection is said to align with paged caches, but the paper explicitly focuses on algorithmic rather than hardware optimization.

key_findings.claim: The meta-token compression extension is conceptual and not empirically validated.
key_findings.evidence: The appendix explains forced emission of a special token and argues that task reward can pressure its KV state to summarize evicted context. No experiment measures accuracy, compression, information retention, or comparison to gist/memento-style summaries, so the claim that this capability comes 'for free' remains a hypothesis.

key_findings.claim: Despite the title's language, this is not catastrophic-forgetting or continual-learning evidence.
key_findings.evidence: 'Forgetting' means irreversible removal of within-generation KV state. The model is trained on one task distribution at a time and evaluated after training; there are no sequential task updates, old-task retention, forward transfer, rehearsal, or model-parameter forgetting metrics.

anchors.section: 3 Resource-use problem and 4 Neural Garbage Collection

method.core_idea: Make KV retention a native stochastic action of the reasoning policy so outcome reward trains both what the model says and which past internal states it preserves.
method.mechanism: Every delta tokens, recent-query attention produces per-layer scores for alive prefix keys. Scores are averaged into fixed blocks; Gumbel top-k samples the retained blocks during training and greedy top-k is used at test. Dr. GRPO applies one group advantage to token and eviction log-probabilities. Per-layer replay masks reconstruct exactly which keys each rollout query saw and recompute live Q/K features for policy gradients. A staircase curriculum increases eviction, and an optional prompt tag conditions behavior on a known budget.
assumptions: Attention from the five latest queries is a useful initialized parameterization of long-term cache utility.
Binary outcome reward supplies enough credit to learn both reasoning tokens and many per-layer subset decisions.
Fixed cadence, block size, and eviction fraction adequately specify the external resource budget.
Per-layer replay masks exactly reproduce rollout state and can be processed without prohibitive systems overhead.
Group-relative Dr. GRPO advantages remain stable with interleaved token and eviction actions and no KL penalty.
A curriculum from mild to aggressive eviction avoids destructive early state shifts.
The memory budget is known at inference for interoceptive conditioning.
Performance on arithmetic and competition math with one 1.5B Qwen-derived model reflects broader resource-management capability.

techniques.role: Bounds steady-state KV size through fixed periodic deletion.
Repurposes existing Q/K attention weights to score cache survival without new parameters.
Samples a tractable fixed-cardinality retained subset with explicit log-probability.
Uses one outcome advantage for generation and per-layer eviction decisions.
Reconstructs state-shifted rollout context during batched policy rescoring.
Stages increasingly aggressive cache deletion during RL.
Conditions reasoning on an explicitly supplied eviction rate.
Proposes an untested special-token channel for consolidating soon-to-be-evicted state.

evaluations.setting: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B trained 250 steps on Countdown; 327,680 training problems, 1,024 held-out tests, cadence 256, 32 prompts by 16 rollouts, maximum completion 1,024
evaluations.metric: Pass@1 and average peak KV-cache reduction
evaluations.result: At reported 2.4x reduction NGC reaches 49.6%, versus KeyDiff 21.2%, SnapKV 7.8%, StreamingLLM 0.2%, and KNorm 0.1%
evaluations.baseline: Four inference-only heuristics on a separately trained full-cache model and a roughly 64% full-cache ceiling

evaluations.metric: Pass@1, reward trajectory, and gradient norm
evaluations.result: Targeted KV Dropout reaches 2.5% and collapses; replay masks without the eviction policy gradient reach 35.7%; full NGC reaches 49.6%
evaluations.baseline: No-eviction training, incorrect causal replay, and token-only objective

evaluations.setting: Budget-aware Countdown evaluation beyond the minimum training cache
evaluations.metric: Pass@1 as a function of peak cache size
evaluations.result: Putting the eviction rate in the prompt improves aggressive-budget accuracy by roughly 8-13 percentage points
evaluations.baseline: Identically trained NGC without a budget tag

evaluations.setting: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B trained 469 steps on DAPO-17k; cadence 350, 256 prompts by 8 rollouts, train max 1,050 and evaluation max 3,850 tokens
evaluations.metric: Pass@32 on AMC 2023, AMC 2025, and AIME 2025 across cache reductions
evaluations.result: NGC leads all four heuristics at 50% per-round eviction and remains near the full-cache ceiling for several 2-3x reduction points; no uncertainty is reported
evaluations.baseline: Full-cache ceiling and the four inference-only heuristics

evaluations.metric: Maximum KV entries immediately before eviction
evaluations.result: The per-layer recurrence c_(t+1)=(1-epsilon)c_t+delta converges to delta/epsilon and total cache to L delta/epsilon
evaluations.baseline: Unbounded linear cache growth without eviction

limitations: Only one DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B model is evaluated; no larger model, alternative architecture, or independent family is tested.
Tasks are confined to Countdown and math competitions; no language modeling, retrieval, coding, science QA, dialogue, tool use, or multimodal context is evaluated.
No independent training seeds, statistical tests, or math-benchmark uncertainty intervals are reported; Countdown only shows one-standard-error bars of unspecified decomposition.

Direct learned compression and RL-guided competitors are omitted, including DMC, DMS, Breadcrumbs, MEMENTO, and the pre-existing outcome-reward method RLKV; all reported baselines are training-free heuristics applied to a full-cache-trained model.
The peak-cache ratio depends on method-specific completion length and does not match generated-token budgets.
No latency, throughput, wall-clock, total-memory, energy, or FLOP measurement validates practical efficiency.
The system learns which state to evict but not cadence or eviction quantity; the core resource allocation remains hand specified.
Interoception presumes a known budget and exposes it in the prompt.
Dense per-layer replay masks may add significant training memory or kernel overhead despite the unmeasured negligible-overhead claim.
The special compression meta-token is proposed without an experiment.
The work does not study catastrophic forgetting, sequential parameter learning, forward transfer, or replay across tasks.
failure_modes: A block containing a low-attention premise can be permanently removed before a later reasoning branch needs it.
Block averaging can hide one crucial token among unimportant neighbors or protect an entire block for one token.
Separate layer decisions can create cross-layer state inconsistency that outcome reward is too sparse to diagnose.
A fixed cadence and fraction can be too aggressive for long dependencies and too conservative for redundant stretches.
Group rewards can provide no eviction gradient when all sampled completions tie.
Greedy top-k at evaluation introduces a train/test action-selection shift from stochastic Gumbel sampling.
A policy trained on one reasoning distribution may retain the wrong features after a task or domain shift.
Prompted budget tags can be ignored, misparsed, or adversarially manipulated.
Reported compression can improve merely because eviction changes completion length rather than because the same computation uses less memory.
Dense replay masks can erase the theoretical cache savings during RL training.
reusable_insights: When an action changes a model's future internal state, policy rescoring must replay that state transition rather than use a richer default context.
Reuse pretrained attention as an initialized control policy, but compare it against learned compression under matched training exposure.
Separate the decision of what to retain from the externally chosen amount and cadence of retention.
Report capability against peak KV bytes, generated tokens, latency, throughput, and total GPU memory on the same trajectories.
Conditioning a policy on a deployment budget can improve one model's Pareto frontier and extrapolation, provided the budget is reliably known.
Use old-domain retention and new-domain adaptation tests before calling a cache policy a general resource-management capability.
A learned consolidation token should be evaluated as a distinct compression channel, not inferred from its theoretical gradient path.
open_questions: Does NGC beat RLKV, DMS, DMC, Breadcrumbs, and MEMENTO when every method receives matched compression-aware training, data, model, cache bytes, generated tokens, and wall-clock?
Can the policy jointly learn eviction amount and cadence under a Lagrangian or constrained-RL cost rather than a fixed environment schedule?
How much training time and total GPU memory do dense per-layer replay masks add at realistic context lengths?
Does an eviction policy trained on math transfer to code, retrieval, dialogue, and agent trajectories without catastrophic state-policy forgetting?
What uncertainty remains after multiple RL seeds and exact-binomial confidence intervals on AIME/AMC?
Can stochastic training and deterministic top-k inference be aligned or calibrated?
Does the proposed meta-token actually consolidate information, and how does it compare to gist tokens, Breadcrumbs, and MEMENTO summaries?
Can compression be evaluated at matched completion content/length so the peak-cache metric cannot be gamed by shorter reasoning?

competitive_landscape.title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: SnapKV selects prompt KV positions per head from an observation window without fine-tuning and reports hardware speed/memory results; NGC learns recurrent generation-time, per-layer block eviction from task reward but lacks systems measurements.

competitive_landscape.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
competitive_landscape.difference: StreamingLLM preserves sinks plus a recent window without training and demonstrates million-token streaming and speedup; NGC uses learned irreversible content selection for reasoning at finite horizons.

competitive_landscape.title: A Simple and Effective L2 Norm-Based Strategy for KV Cache Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: KNorm is training-free, FlashAttention-compatible, and validated on language/retrieval tasks; NGC trains attention scores through outcome reward and is evaluated on reasoning only.

competitive_landscape.title: KeyDiff: Key Similarity-Based KV Cache Eviction for Long-Context LLM Inference in Resource-Constrained Environments
competitive_landscape.difference: KeyDiff uses key geometry without training, supports strict long prompts, and reports latency; NGC instead learns an attention-scored policy and wins on its reasoning tests after compression-aware RL.

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamic Memory Compression: Retrofitting LLMs for Accelerated Inference
competitive_landscape.difference: DMC learns head/layer-specific online compression through continued pretraining, covers 7B-70B models, and reports H100 throughput; NGC uses task-reward RL with discrete block eviction on one 1.5B model.

competitive_landscape.title: Inference-Time Hyper-Scaling with KV Cache Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: Dynamic Memory Sparsification learns per-head delayed eviction in about 1,000 steps across multiple model families and evaluates equal memory reads/latency; NGC uses end-task policy gradients and exact state replay but does not compare against it.

competitive_landscape.title: Breadcrumbs Reasoning: Memory-Efficient Reasoning with Compression Beacons
competitive_landscape.difference: Breadcrumbs periodically writes learned compression beacons and trains them with joint distillation and RL; NGC directly deletes selected blocks using only outcome reward and relegates consolidation tokens to an untested appendix.

competitive_landscape.title: MEMENTO: Teaching LLMs to Manage Their Own Context
competitive_landscape.relationship: Immediate priority threat published ten days earlier
competitive_landscape.difference: MEMENTO teaches explicit block segmentation and dense summaries with two-stage SFT across Qwen, Phi, and Olmo at 8B-32B, plus vLLM throughput; NGC learns selective deletion end-to-end from outcome reward without summary supervision.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens
competitive_landscape.difference: Gist tokens learn prompt compression through modified attention masks and instruction fine-tuning with measured FLOP/wall-time savings; NGC's main method evicts both prompt and generated state, while its gist-like token is only proposed conceptually.

competitive_landscape.title: Which Heads Matter for Reasoning? RL-Guided KV Cache Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: RLKV v1 was submitted on 2025-10-09 and already used GRPO rewards from actual reasoning outcomes to learn which heads require full cache, then reported 20-60% reduction and end-to-end speedup. It freezes the language model, trains L-by-H continuous gates with an auxiliary L1 sparsity penalty, and discretizes them after training; NGC instead jointly updates the LM and samples per-round block survival as native actions using outcome advantage alone.
competitive_landscape.source_version: v3, revised 2026-05-27; priority established by v1

competitive_landscape.title: Hold Onto That Thought: Assessing KV Cache Compression On Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: pre-existing reasoning-cache benchmark and metric warning
competitive_landscape.difference: This multi-model, eight-benchmark study evaluates decoding-time cache compression and shows that low cache budgets can lengthen or derail reasoning traces, so cache bytes alone can trade against extra generation compute. NGC's method-dependent completion-length peak-cache ratio does not neutralize that already documented confound.

competitive_landscape.title: How Much Cache Does Reasoning Need? Depth-Cache Tradeoffs in KV-Compressed Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: This paper was submitted 71 minutes before NGC and studies adaptive versus oblivious cache control through pointer-chasing bounds, explicitly labeling its strongest product lower bound conjectural. It does not learn an eviction policy, but it supplies theoretical resource-capability constraints that NGC's empirical fixed-budget analysis does not test.

competitive_landscape.title: KARA: Efficient Reasoning LLM Serving via Sliding-Window KV Cache Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: KARA uses bidirectional scoring over a recent window, expands selected tokens into flexible chunks, and integrates the policy with PagedAttention in a vLLM-based serving system. It is heuristic rather than outcome-trained, but its explicit throughput implementation is a current systems comparison missing from NGC's cache-proxy-only evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Discovering KV Cache Eviction Policies via LLM-Guided Program Evolution
competitive_landscape.difference: CacheCraft evolves executable eviction scorers and reports that its learned scoring family, rather than chunk structure, drives large RULER gains. Its resulting policy is a fixed prefill scorer rather than an online reasoning action, but it is a current counterexample to the dichotomy between hand-written heuristics and end-to-end weight training.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: NGC is an end-to-end framework in which a model learns to reason and manage its KV cache from outcome reward alone, treating eviction as a native action and using replay masks for correct policy optimization.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Prior work already provides training-free eviction, learned dynamic eviction/compression, learned reasoning summaries, and outcome-driven cache allocation. In particular, RLKV v1 predates NGC by more than six months and uses GRPO reasoning rewards to optimize full-versus-local-cache head gates, although it freezes the LM and adds an L1 resource penalty. MEMENTO predates NGC by ten days and narrows broad 'self-managed context' priority. The distinct checked contribution is therefore the shared outcome-only policy gradient over token generation and stochastic per-layer block survival, together with replay of the cache-induced state shift.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The native discrete eviction action, LM-wide joint update, and replay-mask formulation appear meaningfully novel. The broad idea of learning cache use from outcome reward is not novel after RLKV, and 'resource use as a learned capability' remains broader than the evidence because eviction amount and cadence are externally fixed. A matched comparison against RLKV, DMS, DMC, Breadcrumbs, and MEMENTO with systems metrics is required before claiming a superior learned resource manager.

reviewer_notes: Independently re-read all 22 pages of arXiv:2604.18002v1, including every equation, Figures 1-10, Tables 1-2, references, the cache fixed-point proof, dense replay-mask construction, autograd routing, and untested meta-token appendix. Rendered PDF pages 11-14 were inspected directly to verify all plotted Countdown, ablation, interoception, AMC, and AIME values rather than relying on OCR. The cached PDF is byte-identical to https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.18002v1 and has SHA-256 d962028f6782d287b96b4f0d790b7d45231c7a73676592f7e961bac947747bd3; the source locator and text hash remain exactly those in the generated full-text index. Fourteen version-pinned primary arXiv competitors were checked on 2026-08-23. This second pass materially narrows novelty because RLKV v1 already used reasoning-outcome RL for cache allocation, while preserving NGC's more specific claim to native stochastic token-block eviction with outcome-only joint LM updates and state-faithful replay.

verification.passage_check: Checked every one of 22 PDF pages against the pinned v1 bytes; re-verified Equations 1-7, Figures 1-10, Tables 1-2, and Appendix A.1-A.4. Direct PDF rendering confirmed the 49.6/21.2/7.8/0.2/0.1 Countdown bars, the 2.5/35.7/49.6 ablation, the 8-13 point interoception statement, the plotted pass@32 math values, the delta/epsilon cache fixed point, and the B-by-T-by-T dense per-layer replay masks. The replay claim was qualified as a verified construction rather than an independently executed implementation.
verification.competitor_check: Checked official current arXiv histories and primary abstracts/full HTML for all 14 listed competitors on 2026-08-23, including versions SnapKV v2, StreamingLLM v4, KNorm v4, KeyDiff v4, DMC v2, DMS v2, Breadcrumbs v3, MEMENTO v1, Gist v3, RLKV v3, Hold Onto That Thought v1, Depth-Cache Tradeoffs v1, KARA v2, and CacheCraft v1.
